failures.title: Jeep EZD 5.7 HEMI Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: MDS lifter failure and camshaft lobe wear - the "HEMI Tick"
items.whatHappens: The 5.7 HEMI uses the Multi-Displacement System (MDS) to deactivate four cylinders under light load. The MDS lifters are complex and can fail, leading to a ticking noise (the "HEMI tick") that progresses to camshaft lobe wear if ignored. If a lifter fails, it can also cause a misfire code .
items.repairVsReplace: Lifter and camshaft replacement is a significant top-end job (£1,800-£3,000 at an independent). If the camshaft lobe is worn, the camshaft must be replaced - which typically requires engine removal on Grand Cherokee WK models due to the front differential position. This can push costs into the £3,000-£5,000 range, approaching the cost of a reconditioned engine.

items.title: Exhaust manifold stud breakage - all years
items.whatHappens: The exhaust manifold studs on the 5.7 HEMI are prone to breaking due to heat cycling. This causes exhaust leaks, resulting in a ticking noise (often confused with the "HEMI tick"), and can lead to reduced fuel economy and engine performance .
items.repairVsReplace: Manifold stud extraction and replacement is a labour-intensive job (£600-£1,200) as broken studs often require drilling out. Upgrading to ARP studs is a common preventative fix.

items.title: Water pump failure - coolant leaks
items.whatHappens: The water pump on the 5.7 HEMI can fail, causing coolant leaks and overheating. The pump is belt-driven and located at the front of the engine, which makes it accessible but can be challenging in the tight engine bay of the Grand Cherokee WK .
items.repairVsReplace: Water pump replacement is a manageable job (£300-£600 at an independent). If the engine has overheated due to pump failure, head gasket or cylinder head damage may have occurred.

items.title: Oil pan gasket leaks
items.whatHappens: The oil pan gasket on the 5.7 HEMI can fail, causing oil leaks. The cast-iron block and aluminium sump expand at different rates, and the gasket can deteriorate over time .
items.repairVsReplace: Oil pan gasket replacement is a labour-intensive job (£400-£800) as the engine must be supported and the front differential (on Grand Cherokee WK) may need to be moved.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 5.7 HEMI was updated throughout its production run. The EZD (2005-2012) is part of the second-generation HEMI (GEN II) with improved power output and emissions. However, the MDS lifter issue and exhaust manifold stud problems remain across all years. Regular oil changes (every 5,000 miles) using the correct 5W-20 or 5W-30 synthetic oil is essential for MDS lifter health.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the EZD 5.7 HEMI
variants.intro: The EZD is one of several codes in Chrysler's HEMI family. The 5.7 HEMI has evolved through multiple generations, and understanding the differences matters when buying a replacement. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped label on the front or side of the V8 - On the V5C registration document under "Engine number" - On the driver's door pillar or under-bonnet VIN/engine sticker - Via a VIN decoder - enter your full 17-digit VIN online to confirm the factory engine code Common confusions: | Similar code | Difference | Link | |--------------|------------|------| | EZC | 5.7 HEMI variant with different ECU calibration (2003-2008 Chrysler/Dodge applications) | [EZC engine] | | EZG | 5.7 HEMI variant with different emissions hardware | [EZG engine] | | EZH | 5.7 HEMI variant - often used in Ram/Dodge applications with different sump and ancillaries | [EZH engine] | | EHB / ERC / EXF | 2.0 Hurricane / 3.6 Pentastar / 3.0 EcoDiesel - completely different engines | See previous pages |

relatives.description: the 4.7-litre V8 that preceded the HEMI in Grand Cherokee WK and other Chrysler/Jeep applications. The HEMI replaced it with significantly more power (326 hp vs 235 hp) and the MDS cylinder-deactivation system, but also introduced greater complexity and the MDS lifter failure risk. [Link to 4.7L PowerTech engine]

It powers the Chrysler 300C (2005-2014), Dodge Charger (2006-present), Dodge Challenger (2008-present), Dodge Durango (2006-present), and Ram 1500 (2003-2019). If sourcing a used unit, confirm the donor vehicle's engine code matches your EZD exactly

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EZD 5.7 HEMI - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used EZD can make sense for older Grand Cherokee or Commander examples where vehicle value doesn't justify a recon unit. However - insist on documented service history and evidence that the MDS lifters have been addressed. The "HEMI Tick" is a red flag; walk away from any unit with ticking noise on cold start or idle. Exhaust manifold stud condition is also critical; broken studs are common and add cost. Given the age of these engines (2005-2012), many used units are high-mileage and near the end of their service life.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper EZD recon addresses the known weak points - MDS lifters are replaced with updated units, the camshaft is inspected and replaced if worn, exhaust manifold studs are replaced with upgraded hardware, and all gaskets and seals are renewed. The oil pump and water pump are also inspected or replaced. With 12-24 months warranty, this is the safest route for most owners, particularly as these engines approach 15-20 years old and used units are increasingly hard to find with good history.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild of the EZD is usually only justified for low-mileage, high-value examples (e.g., a cherished Grand Cherokee WK Overland with under 60,000 miles). The rebuild must include new MDS lifters, new camshaft, new timing chain and tensioner, new water pump, new oil pump, and new pistons and rings. This is the "zero-risk" option - but at £5,500-£8,000 supply-only, it's only viable for vehicles worth over £10,000.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Fitting through our network of vetted UK Jeep and V8 specialists - supply-only or full supply and fit, with nationwide delivery and warranty cover on every reconditioned and rebuilt unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The EZD sits in vehicles with modest value ranges in 2025 - a 2005 Grand Cherokee WK 5.7 HEMI may be worth £3,000-£6,000, while a 2010 Commander might be worth £2,000-£5,000. Given these values, evaluate carefully before committing to a replacement. A used engine with documented MDS lifter history may be the only financially sensible option for lower-value examples. If the vehicle is worth less than £4,000, consider whether a replacement is justified at all - a £3,500 reconditioned engine plus £1,000 labour could easily exceed the vehicle's value. Always factor in the full fitted cost before proceeding. These are iconic engines but the value of the host vehicles often does not justify expensive replacements.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Jeep EZD 5.7 HEMI engine?
items.answer: The most common and expensive failure is the MDS lifter and camshaft lobe wear, known as the 'HEMI Tick'. Typical onset is 80,000-120,000 miles. If ignored, it progresses to camshaft lobe wear and misfire codes. Lifter and camshaft replacement costs £1,800-£3,000; if the camshaft is worn, engine removal is often required. The exhaust manifold studs also commonly break, causing exhaust leaks.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned EZD 5.7 HEMI engine?
items.answer: A used EZD is viable only if it has full documented service history and evidence that the MDS lifters have been replaced with updated units. The "HEMI Tick" is a red flag - walk away from any unit with ticking noise on cold start. Given the age of these engines (2005-2012), many used units are high-mileage and near the end of their service life. A reconditioned unit is the better choice for most owners, as it addresses the MDS lifters, camshaft, exhaust manifold studs, and includes a 12-24 month warranty. However, always factor in the vehicle's value - a £3,500 recon plus labour may exceed the value of a £4,000 Grand Cherokee. Browse reconditioned EZD engines with warranty.

items.question: What is the difference between EZD, EZC, and EZH HEMI engines?
items.answer: They are all 5.7 HEMI variants but have different specifications. EZD is the 5.7 HEMI fitted to Jeep Grand Cherokee WK and Commander (326 hp). EZC is an earlier variant (2003-2008) used in Chrysler 300C and Dodge applications with different ECU calibration. EZH is a variant used in Ram/Dodge applications with different sump orientation and ancillaries. Always confirm your exact code before ordering - fitting the wrong variant may require reprogramming or different ancillaries.

EZC: earlier variant (2003-2008) used in Chrysler 300C and Dodge applications; different ECU calibration

items.question: How do I confirm my Jeep has the EZD engine code?
items.answer: Check three places: the engine block itself (a stamped label on the front or side of the V8), your V5C registration document under 'Engine number', and use a VIN decoder online with your full 17-digit VIN to pull the factory build sheet. Given the confusion with other 5.7 HEMI codes, always verify the physical label before ordering.
